Revised assessment: The statement conveys modest growth with a tight labor market but persistent, elevated inflation; the 25 bp hike to 5–5.25% and continued balance-sheet runoff reflect a forward-looking, inflation-forecast-targeting stance that prioritizes inflation expectations (Svensson 1997; Svensson and Woodford 1999). The focus on “cumulative tightening” and “lags” aligns with New Keynesian IS/Phillips mechanisms and rule-based identification of policy (Lubik and Schorfheide 2004; Rudebusch). The warning that tighter bank credit will weigh on activity is consistent with the credit/bank-lending channel literature (Bernanke’s broad credit channel; Kashyap), implying near-term growth headwinds despite a “sound” banking system. Sticky-information dynamics suggest inflation persistence (Mankiw and Reis 2002), justifying the Committee’s “highly attentive” tone on inflation risks. Net tone: cautiously hawkish given inflation persistence and credit tightening, tempered by robust employment.
